newsitem.title: USA: BPA hopes to win bid to raise intertie power flow.
newsitem.headline: BPA hopes to win bid to raise intertie power flow.

text.p: Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) will meet Friday with Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) to review plans to raise the amount of electricity flowing on major interstate power lines.
Operation of the lines was cut to 65 percent capacity in August after two major power outages hit the West last summer.
The agencies met earlier this month, but BPA was instructed to carry out additional system studies.
BPA hopes to raise transmission capacity on lines running between the Pacific Northwest and California by 25 percent by mid-February.
The federal power marketing agency also plans to install new equipment to allow capacity to rise in stages to full rates in time for the April runoff, when hydroelectric dam output increases.
If the additional studies answer the WSCC's remaining concerns, the plan will be forwarded to the WSCC board of trustees which has 10 days to accept or reject it, BPA spokeswoman Crystal Ball said.
She noted BPA has committed to increasing the "megavars" or voltage support available to the tranmission system by 50 percent in the event of a major line outage.
In the past, BPA has provided such support at no cost, but plans to eventually start charging utilities for the service, Ball said.
The AC segment of the intertie has a rated capacity 4,800 megawatts (MW), compared with a current limit of 3,200 MW. The DC line is rated at 3,200 MW, but was limited to 2,000 MW.
